Alvotech is an Icelandic biotechnology company, based in Reykjavik, that develops and manufactures biosimilar medicines, including versions of Humira and Stelara, with partners selling them in Europe, the US and other markets. Customers are partner pharmaceutical companies and health systems. It is listed on Nasdaq (ALVO) and Nasdaq Iceland, and is majority-controlled by Alvogen founder Robert Wessman. Crunchbase shows about 2.2 billion dollars of funding. B2B pharmaceutical brand, widely known in Iceland.

Amyris was an Emeryville, California synthetic biology company that used engineered yeast to produce ingredients and consumer products, including squalane, sweeteners and cosmetics, and ran consumer beauty brands such as Biossance, Pipette and Rose Inc. It was listed on Nasdaq (AMRS) and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in August 2023, selling off its brands and assets. Crunchbase shows about 1.9 billion dollars of funding. Biossance gave it some consumer visibility, but the company has since been restructured.

Endo Pharmaceuticals is a Pennsylvania-based specialty pharmaceutical company, headquartered in Malvern, that develops and sells branded and generic drugs, including Aveed, Xiaflex and Supprelin, through its Endo Specialty Therapeutics and Par Pharmaceutical units. It filed for Chapter 11 in 2022, emerged in 2024 as a new Endo, Inc., and agreed a merger with Mallinckrodt in 2025. Customers are wholesalers, pharmacies and hospitals. Crunchbase shows about 2 billion dollars of funding. B2B pharma brand with limited consumer awareness.

Exact Sciences is a Madison, Wisconsin diagnostics company known for Cologuard, a non-invasive stool-based colon cancer screening test, and Oncotype DX genomic tests for breast cancer, along with other cancer testing products. Customers are patients, physicians and health insurers, with revenue of more than 2 billion dollars. Listed on Nasdaq (EXAS). Crunchbase shows about 2.75 billion dollars of funding. Cologuard is widely advertised to US consumers aged 45 and over, so brand awareness is high.

Haemonetics is a Boston-area medical technology company that makes devices and consumables for blood and plasma collection, plasma-derived product processing, hospital transfusion and cardiac and vascular care, including NexSys PCS and TEG testing. Customers are plasma collectors, blood banks and hospitals worldwide, and revenue is about 1.3 billion dollars. Listed on the NYSE (HAE). Crunchbase shows about 1.75 billion dollars of funding. B2B healthcare brand with no consumer awareness.

Harmony Biosciences is a Pennsylvania-based pharmaceutical company, in Plymouth Meeting, which markets Wakix (pitolisant) for excessive daytime sleepiness and cataplexy in narcolepsy, and develops other drugs for rare neurological conditions. Customers are patients, sleep specialists and pharmacies, and revenue is product sales of several hundred million dollars a year. Listed on Nasdaq (HRMY). Crunchbase shows about 1.7 billion dollars of funding. Specialist pharma brand with low consumer awareness.

Intra-Cellular Therapies was a New Jersey biopharma company, based in Bedminster, that developed and sold Caplyta (lumateperone) for schizophrenia, bipolar depression and later major depressive disorder. Customers were patients, psychiatrists and pharmacies, with revenue exceeding 600 million dollars a year. Johnson & Johnson acquired the company for about 14.6 billion dollars in 2025. Crunchbase shows about 2.3 billion dollars of funding. Specialist pharma brand with little consumer awareness, now part of J&J.

Revance Therapeutics was a Nashville-based aesthetics and therapeutics biotech that sold Daxxify, a long-lasting botulinum toxin for frown lines and cervical dystonia, and the RHA dermal filler line distributed in the US, plus the Opul beauty-customer platform. Customers were dermatologists, plastic surgeons and patients. Crown Laboratories acquired it in 2025 for about 924 million dollars, after the company had been listed on Nasdaq (RVNC). Crunchbase shows about 1.7 billion dollars of funding. Consumer-facing aesthetics brand.

Smith & Nephew is a UK medical technology company, headquartered in Watford, England, that makes orthopaedic implants for knee and hip replacement, sports medicine and arthroscopy equipment, and advanced wound care products such as Allevyn and Santyl. Customers are hospitals, surgeons and health systems, with revenue of about 5.5 billion dollars. Founded in 1856, it employs around 18,000 people and is listed on the London Stock Exchange (SN) and NYSE (SNN). Crunchbase shows about 1.67 billion dollars of funding. B2B healthcare brand with some consumer awareness.

UPM-Kymmene is a Finnish forest industry group, headquartered in Helsinki, that produces pulp, paper, specialty labels (UPM Raflatac), plywood and timber, and renewable fuels and biochemicals from wood. Customers are packaging, printing, construction and fuel industries globally. It is a major forest owner, employs around 17,000 people and has revenue of about 10 billion euros. Listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (UPM). Crunchbase shows about 1.85 billion in funding. B2B industrial brand with strong recognition in Finland, though little among consumers elsewhere.

89bio was a San Francisco-based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing pegozafermin for the liver disease MASH (metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis) and severe hypertriglyceridemia, with no product on the market. It was listed on Nasdaq (ETNB), and Roche agreed to acquire it in 2025 for several billion dollars. Customers would be hospitals and patients if approved, and funding came from equity markets. Crunchbase shows about 1.19 billion dollars of funding. Biotech brand with no consumer awareness.

Biocon Biologics is the Bengaluru-based biosimilars subsidiary of Biocon, selling insulin, oncology and immunology biosimilars such as trastuzumab and adalimumab in more than 100 countries, and it combined with the biosimilars business of Viatris in 2022. Customers are hospitals, health systems and pharmacies. It is controlled by Biocon, founded by Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, and is an unlisted company. Crunchbase shows about 1.3 billion dollars of funding. B2B pharma brand with little consumer awareness, though known in India.

BioSig Technologies is a Florida-based medical technology company, in Winter Park, which developed the PURE EP signal-processing system that gives cardiologists clearer cardiac signals during ablation procedures for heart rhythm disorders. Customers are hospitals and electrophysiology labs, and revenue has been small. It is listed on Nasdaq (BSGM). Crunchbase shows about 1.2 billion dollars of funding, which looks inflated or a data issue. Micro-cap medical device brand with no consumer awareness.

Bruntwood SciTech is a joint venture of Manchester-based property company Bruntwood and Legal & General, creating science and technology innovation districts and workspace for life sciences, digital and tech companies in Manchester, Birmingham, Leeds, Liverpool and Cheshire (Alderley Park). Tenants are start-ups, scale-ups and research organisations, and revenue comes from rents and services. Crunchbase shows about 1.08 billion in funding in 2025. B2B property brand with strong regional visibility in northern England.

Cidara Therapeutics is a San Diego biotechnology company developing long-acting antiviral drug conjugates for influenza prevention and treatment, and previously the antifungal rezafungin, which was licensed to Mundipharma and Melinta. Customers would be health systems and patients, and revenue has come from licensing and collaboration deals. Listed on Nasdaq (CDTX). Crunchbase shows about 1.26 billion dollars of funding in 2025. Biotech brand with no consumer awareness.

Cogent Biosciences is a Waltham, Massachusetts clinical-stage biotechnology company developing bezuclastinib, a drug for systemic mastocytosis and gastrointestinal stromal tumours, along with other targeted therapies for genetically defined diseases. It has no approved product yet and is listed on Nasdaq (COGT). Funding comes from equity markets and collaborations, and Crunchbase shows about 1.6 billion dollars. B2B biotech brand with no consumer awareness.

Denali Therapeutics is a South San Francisco biotechnology company developing treatments for neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson's, Alzheimer's and Hunter syndrome, using a blood-brain barrier transport vehicle platform. Customers would be patients and health systems if drugs are approved, and it has collaborations with Biogen and Sanofi. Listed on Nasdaq (DNLI). Crunchbase shows about 1.3 billion dollars of funding. Biotech brand with no consumer awareness.

Dynavax Technologies is an Emeryville, California biopharmaceutical company that makes Heplisav-B, an adult hepatitis B vaccine, and develops shingles and other vaccine candidates using its CpG 1018 adjuvant, which was also used in some COVID-19 vaccines. Customers are health systems, pharmacies and governments. Listed on Nasdaq (DVAX). Crunchbase shows about 1.58 billion dollars of funding. Specialist pharma brand with limited consumer awareness.

Heron Therapeutics is a North Carolina-based pharmaceutical company, in Cary, selling pain and nausea medicines, including Zynrelef for post-surgical pain, Aponvie and Cinvanti for chemotherapy-related nausea, and Sustol. Customers are hospitals, surgical centres and oncology clinics, with revenue of around 150 million dollars a year. Listed on Nasdaq (HRTX). Crunchbase shows about 1.17 billion dollars of funding. Specialist pharma brand with no consumer awareness.

Innovent Biologics is a Chinese biopharmaceutical company, based in Suzhou, that develops and sells antibody-based medicines for cancer, metabolic and autoimmune diseases, including Tyvyt (sintilimab) and weight-loss drug mazdutide. Customers are hospitals and patients in China, and it partners with Eli Lilly. Founded in 2011, it is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (1801). Crunchbase shows about 1.5 billion dollars of funding. Healthcare brand with strong profile in China's pharma sector.

Kodiak Sciences is a Palo Alto, California clinical-stage biotechnology company developing treatments for retinal diseases such as wet age-related macular degeneration and diabetic eye disease, using its antibody biopolymer conjugate platform, including tarcocimab tedromer. It has no approved product and is listed on Nasdaq (KOD). Funding comes from equity markets, and Crunchbase shows about 1.2 billion dollars. B2B biotech brand with no consumer awareness.

Merus is a Utrecht, Netherlands-based clinical-stage oncology company that develops multispecific antibody medicines using its Biclonics technology, with the lead candidate petosemtamab for head and neck and colorectal cancers. It was listed on Nasdaq (MRUS) and Genmab agreed to acquire it in 2025 for several billion dollars. Customers would be hospitals and cancer patients. Crunchbase shows about 1.37 billion dollars of funding. Biotech brand with no consumer awareness.

Ocular Therapeutix is a Bedford, Massachusetts biopharmaceutical company that makes Dextenza, an intracanalicular insert for post-surgery eye pain and inflammation, and ReSure Sealant, and develops Axpaxli (OTX-TKI) for wet age-related macular degeneration. Customers are eye surgeons, surgical centres and patients. Listed on Nasdaq (OCUL). Crunchbase shows about 1.19 billion dollars of funding. Specialist ophthalmology brand with no consumer awareness, though known to eye surgeons and retina specialists in the US.

Rhythm Pharmaceuticals is a Boston biopharmaceutical company that markets Imcivree (setmelanotide) for rare genetic forms of obesity, including POMC deficiency and Bardet-Biedl syndrome, and is developing it for hypothalamic obesity. Customers are patients and specialist physicians through pharmacies, and revenue is product sales of a hundred million dollars or so. Listed on Nasdaq (RYTM). Crunchbase shows about 1.2 billion dollars of funding. Specialist pharma brand with no consumer awareness.

Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical is a Novato, California biopharmaceutical company specialising in rare and ultra-rare genetic diseases, with marketed medicines such as Crysvita for X-linked hypophosphatemia, Mepsevii, Dojolvi and Evkeeza (ex-US), and gene therapy candidates in development. Customers are patients, specialists and health systems, and revenue is over 500 million dollars a year. Listed on Nasdaq (RARE). Crunchbase shows about 1.54 billion dollars of funding. Specialist pharma brand with no consumer awareness.

Vera Therapeutics is a Brisbane, California clinical-stage biotechnology company developing atacicept for IgA nephropathy and other immune-mediated kidney diseases, which it sought US approval for. It is listed on Nasdaq (VERA) and funded by equity markets, with no product on the market at last report. Crunchbase shows about 1.23 billion dollars of funding. Biotech brand with no consumer awareness, and revenue only if approval and launch succeed.

Wave Life Sciences is a Cambridge, Massachusetts and Singapore-based clinical-stage RNA medicines company that develops oligonucleotide therapeutics, including RNA editing and splicing candidates for conditions such as alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, obesity and Huntington's disease, using its PRISM platform. It partners with GSK and Takeda, and is listed on Nasdaq (WVE). Crunchbase shows about 1.2 billion dollars of funding. B2B biotech brand with no consumer awareness.

ADMA Biologics is a Ramsey, New Jersey biopharmaceutical company that makes and sells plasma-derived immune globulin products, including Asceniv, Bivigam and Nabi-HB, for patients with primary immunodeficiency and related conditions, and runs plasma collection centres. Customers are specialty distributors, hospitals and clinics. Listed on Nasdaq (ADMA). Crunchbase shows about 1.06 billion dollars of funding. Specialist pharma brand with no consumer awareness.

Apellis Pharmaceuticals is a Waltham, Massachusetts biopharmaceutical company that markets Syfovre, the first approved treatment for geographic atrophy secondary to age-related macular degeneration, and Empaveli, for the rare blood disorder PNH and certain kidney diseases. Customers are retina specialists, haematologists and patients. Listed on Nasdaq (APLS), with revenue of several hundred million dollars. Crunchbase shows about 920 million dollars of funding. Specialist pharma brand with no consumer awareness.

Axsome Therapeutics is a New York-based biopharmaceutical company that markets Auvelity for major depressive disorder, Sunosi for excessive sleepiness, and Symbravo for migraine, and develops other treatments for central nervous system disorders. Customers are psychiatrists, neurologists and patients through pharmacies. Listed on Nasdaq (AXSM), with revenue of several hundred million dollars. Crunchbase shows about 1.05 billion dollars of funding. Specialist pharma brand with limited consumer awareness.

Bruker is a Billerica, Massachusetts maker of scientific instruments, including mass spectrometers, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) systems, X-ray, microscopy and preclinical imaging equipment, sold to universities, pharmaceutical firms, hospitals and industry. It has around 11,000 employees and revenue of about 3 billion dollars. Listed on Nasdaq (BRKR). Crunchbase shows about 1 billion dollars of funding. B2B scientific instruments brand with no consumer awareness.

Centessa Pharmaceuticals is a clinical-stage biotechnology company with offices in Cambridge, Massachusetts and the UK, developing orexin receptor agonists such as ORX750 for narcolepsy and other sleep disorders. It has no approved product and is listed on Nasdaq (CNTA). Funding comes from equity markets, and Crunchbase shows about 1.13 billion dollars. B2B biotech brand with no consumer awareness, and no product revenue until a medicine is approved and launched.

Eikon Therapeutics is a biotechnology company in the San Francisco Bay area, in Millbrae, California, founded in 2019 and led by Roger Perlmutter, formerly head of research at Merck. It uses super-resolution microscopy to track single molecules in living cells for discovering cancer and immune drugs. Customers would be patients and health systems if drugs are approved. It is privately held, and Crunchbase shows about 1.12 billion dollars of funding. B2B biotech brand with no consumer awareness.

about: FFF Enterprises is a Temecula, California pharmaceutical distributor, one of the largest in the US for plasma products, vaccines, biosimilars and specialty drugs, serving hospitals, physicians, clinics and pharmacies. Founded in 1988, it supplies public and private healthcare customers, and revenue is several billion dollars from drug distribution. It is privately held. Crunchbase shows about 1.12 billion dollars of funding in 2025, likely a financing. B2B healthcare distributor with no consumer profile.

HAYA Therapeutics is a Lausanne, Switzerland-based biotechnology company developing RNA-targeted therapies based on long non-coding RNAs, aimed at heart disease and age-related conditions. Customers would be patients and health systems if drugs are approved. It is venture-backed and privately held, with Crunchbase showing about 1.1 billion dollars of funding, which looks high for a company at this stage. B2B biotech brand with no consumer awareness. Check funding figure before outreach.

It began in China, later moved its headquarters to Rockville, Maryland, and is listed on Nasdaq (IMAB). It earns no meaningful product sales yet and is funded by equity raises and partnerships; Crunchbase shows about $880 million raised in total. Ultimate customers would be hospitals and patients, but today it deals with pharma partners and investors. B2B biotech with little consumer brand awareness.

It is listed on Nasdaq (IMNM) and has no large commercial revenue; it funds itself through equity offerings, with Crunchbase showing roughly $1 billion raised in total. Future customers are oncologists, hospitals and health systems. A biotech with no consumer brand awareness and limited relevance outside investor and healthcare circles.

about: Isotopen Technologien Muenchen (ITM) is a radiopharmaceutical company based in Garching near Munich, Germany, developing and supplying targeted radionuclide therapies for cancer, including its lead candidate ITM-11 (lutetium-177 edotreotide) for neuroendocrine tumours, and supplying medical isotopes such as lutetium-177. Customers are hospitals, nuclear medicine departments and pharma partners. It is privately held and has raised large private rounds, roughly $1 billion in total per Crunchbase, including a 2025 financing. B2B pharma and isotope supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

about: Kailera Therapeutics is a US biotech based in Waltham, Massachusetts, developing next-generation injectable and oral treatments for obesity and related metabolic conditions, working with GLP-1 type drug candidates licensed from Chinese developer Hengrui. It launched in 2024 and raised a large Series B of about $600 million, with roughly $1 billion in total funding. It has no marketed product yet; revenue would come from drug sales to patients through healthcare systems. Private, venture-backed. No consumer brand yet, but it targets the very large obesity-drug market.

It is private and venture-backed, with about $920 million raised in total per Crunchbase, including a large 2025 round. It has no marketed product yet and earns no meaningful revenue. Future customers are patients via hospitals and health systems. A B2B biotech with no consumer brand awareness.

about: Omeros is a Seattle-based biopharmaceutical company focused on drugs for complement-mediated and other immune disorders, with its lead candidate narsoplimab (a MASP-2 inhibitor) for transplant-associated thrombotic microangiopathy. It previously sold the eye-surgery drug Omidria, which it sold to Rayner in 2021. Listed on Nasdaq (OMER). Revenue is limited and the company relies on equity raising and royalties, with about $1 billion raised in total per Crunchbase. Customers are hospitals and specialist physicians. B2B pharma with very little consumer brand awareness.

about: Prometheus Biosciences was a San Diego biotech developing precision treatments for inflammatory bowel disease, especially an antibody against TL1A for ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, plus diagnostic tests for IBD. It listed on Nasdaq in 2021 and was acquired by Merck for about $10.8 billion in a deal announced in April 2023 and completed in June 2023, so it is now part of Merck. Crunchbase funding shows roughly $950 million. Customers were gastroenterologists and patients. It had no consumer brand awareness and no longer operates independently.

Terns Pharmaceuticals is a clinical-stage biotech in Foster City, California, developing oral small-molecule drugs for metabolic disease and cancer, including a GLP-1 receptor agonist for obesity and a BCR-ABL inhibitor for chronic myeloid leukaemia. It is listed on Nasdaq (TERN). It has no marketed product, so revenue is minimal and it funds operations through equity offerings, with Crunchbase showing about $1.1 billion raised in total. Future customers are patients via health systems. A B2B biotech with little consumer awareness, but exposure to the fast-growing obesity-drug theme.

A research-stage company with no consumer brand and no sponsorship use.

about: Annexon Biosciences is a South San Francisco clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, founded in 2011, developing complement-inhibiting antibody drugs for neurological, ophthalmic and autoimmune diseases, such as Guillain-Barre syndrome and geographic atrophy. It is listed on Nasdaq as ANNX and has no approved product, so it earns no product revenue and relies on financing. Crunchbase shows about 770 million dollars raised. A science-driven business with no consumer brand profile, so sponsorship fit is minimal.

Aura Biosciences is a Boston-area clinical-stage biotechnology company, founded in 2009, developing bel-sar, a light-activated virus-like drug conjugate for eye cancers such as choroidal melanoma and other cancers. It is listed on Nasdaq as AURA, has no approved product and relies on investors, with Crunchbase showing about 756 million dollars raised. A research-stage business with no consumer brand and little relevance as a sponsor.

A private research-stage company with no consumer brand awareness.

about: Cellares is a South San Francisco company, founded in 2018, that builds automated manufacturing platforms for cell therapies, including the Cell Shuttle, and operates as an integrated development and manufacturing organisation, serving drugmakers producing CAR-T and similar treatments. It earns revenue from manufacturing contracts and technology deals with large pharma. Crunchbase shows about 682 million dollars raised from investors such as SoftBank and Eclipse. A B2B life-sciences business with no consumer profile.
